subject: bicycle
reasoning:
I'm planning out a vintage bicycle model using the SDK, setting up a root joint plus wheel, steering, and crank joints to structure the parts, with wheel radius around 0.34 to match a 28" roadster.

Now I'm working out the frame geometry—placing the bottom bracket, seat tube, and head tube positions along a 1.1m wheelbase, front wheel at z=+0.55 and rear at z=-0.55, and calculating the head tube angle (~70°) by tracing the steering axis from the front axle up to the head tube top to get realistic fork geometry.

I'm laying out the top tube, down tube, seat stays, and chain stays as rod segments connecting BB, seat tube, head tube, and rear axle, mirrored at ±0.06 for left/right sides, and planning joint definitions (root at BB, frontWheel joint) so each rod attaches to an explicit bone rather than relying on nearest-joint defaults.

I'm defining the remaining joints for rear wheel, steering axis, crank, pedals, and seat, then setting parts to parent from root or the steer joint for the fork. For the wheels, I'm constructing tires and rims as rotated torus geometries and planning 36 thin spoke rods per wheel, treating each as a separate part.

I'm working out spoke placement—alternating hub flange offsets with slight tangential angles, using low-poly triangular cross-sections to keep the mesh efficient—plus hub cylinders and tire coloring choices (dark tire, chrome rim, considering a whitewall accent). Now I'm thinking through fender construction options using partial torus or open cylinder geometry to get that curved vintage look.

Still refining the fender geometry...

I'm working out the arc angles and rotation directions so the front fender mirrors the rear one correctly, using a 150° arc and flipping the Y rotation sign to get the curve opening toward the front wheel.

Now I'm moving to the handlebars, setting up the stem position above the head tube and defining a swept north-road bar shape with symmetrical control points for the left and right grips.

Working out the saddle shape with a narrow nose and wider back, positioning it near the seat post, then starting on the spring supports underneath.

Now I'm placing the seatpost rod extending from the seat tube top up to the saddle mount point, keeping the angle consistent with the frame's seat tube.

For the drivetrain, I'm setting up the chainring as a flat cylinder on the drive side (-X), sized around 0.09 radius with thin thickness, and planning the rear cog to match.

Then I'm adding chain rods connecting the top and bottom of the chainring to the rear cog, and building out the crank arms and pedals — right crank down, left crank up for a natural resting pose, with pedal boxes attached at the arm ends and a spindle rod running through the bottom bracket.

Skipping a chain guard and kickstand for simplicity, I'm adding a small rear rack above the fender with two support struts down to the rear axle, plus a tiny red rear reflector. For colors, I'm going with a deep racing green frame, cream accents, chrome fittings, and leather-brown trim.

Working out the whitewall tire look...

Good enough, settling on a thin ring positioned just inside the tire surface at x=0.0238, visible but simple. Now moving on to building the wheel function with spokes arranged radially in a loop of 36 segments.

Computing spoke geometry and rod placement...

Now I'm working out the steerer and head tube placement with a joint at the steer axis, then planning the hierarchy: fork and front wheel as children of the steer joint, with root holding the frame, rear wheel, crank, and pedals.

Placing the stem and handlebar geometry, sketching coordinates for a north-road style bar sweeping back toward the rider.

Adding small details: a cream bell sphere mounted on the bar, and a chrome lamp with a bracket rod near the fork crown, including a pale yellow cylindrical lens pointing forward.

Now I'm positioning the drivetrain and pedals -- working out crank arm placement and rotation from the bottom bracket to each pedal, sizing the pedal boxes, and checking that the lowest points (tire bottom, pedal bottoms) sit correctly above the floor level.

I'm also adding a rear rack platform and reflector, calculating their heights relative to the rear fender top so the rack sits just above the fender and the seat stays pass through cleanly.

Now I'm working out the struts connecting the rack to the axle and seat stays, estimating intersection points along the seat stay line to position each support rod reasonably.

Chainstays run from the bottom bracket to the rear axle, and I'm adding cream-colored lug details at joints — head tube caps, a seat lug sphere, and a chrome bottom bracket shell cylinder — to give the frame authentic construction details before writing the rod-building helper function.
